sentences.text: Brochuchus possessed a flat, relatively narrow skull and measured larger than the dwarf crocodile yet smaller than most modern crocodiles.
Scientists describe this animal as the most generalist member of the Osteolaeminae clade, a group characterized by a long snout.
If it preyed on apes, Brochuchus could be one of the earliest known "ape-eating" crocodilians.
The genus Brochuchus was named by Conrad and colleagues in 2013.
Fossils of Brochuchus have been found in the Hiwegi Formation on Rusinga Island in Lake Victoria, Kenya.
Brochuchus was likely a predatory animal that spent most of its time in water.
Researchers suggest Brochuchus may have preyed on the early ape Proconsul, though there is no direct fossil evidence of its diet.
Brochuchus is classified within the crocodile family Crocodylidae.
Brochuchus belongs to the subfamily Osteolaeminae within the family Crocodylidae.
Brochuchus lived during the Early Miocene epoch.
Brochuchus lived between 20.45 and 13.82 million years ago, spanning the Burdigalian to Langhian stages.
